problems.field: eligibility.criterion_2_at_least_50_people (affirmative conclusion under challenge; also checked S2 and S3)
problems.source_says: The affirmative claim that at least 50 distinct people were analyzed is not explicitly supported. S1 randomized and analyzed 180,324 employer accounts, S2 reports 101,601 employers, and S3 reports 525,119 new employers; none supplies a distinct-person count or a mapping between accounts and people. The text-outcome counts are posts. The saved final form already leaves people counts null and marks criterion 2 unclear, so this is an evidence gap in the positive conclusion posed in the brief, not a miscopied numerical people count in the current form.
problems.quote: Each employer account is randomized only at their ﬁrst attempt to create a job post; subsequent attempts keep the same assignment.
problems.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 3 (account-level assignment); p. 26, Table 3; p. 56, Table 21; p. 66, Appendix B; p. 72, Table 36; p. 68, Figure 15 notes. Full markdown read through p. 72, including both appendices; no distinct-person mapping found. Codebook Sections 3 and 7 require people counts.

confirmed.statement: S1 assigns 90,048 treatment and 90,276 control employer accounts once, retaining assignment on later attempts; their sum is 180,324.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 3; p. 55, Figure 12; p. 56, Table 21.

confirmed.statement: S1 unconditional analyses retain 180,324 accounts, including non-posters; Table 21 gives the same 90,276 control and 90,048 treatment denominators. No reduction from the reported allocation total is evident in this analysis.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 26, Table 3 and notes; p. 56, Table 21, Job posting rate rows.

confirmed.statement: S1 first-post analyses use 58,495 posts within 14 days: 26,781 control and 31,714 treatment. One observation is an employer account's first post, not an additional person for each text or comparison pair.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, Table 1 and notes; p. 56, Table 21, Number of words in job post rows.

confirmed.statement: Derived non-posting counts are 63,495 control (90,276 minus 26,781) and 58,334 treatment (90,048 minus 31,714). These accounts remain in the unconditional analysis; conditioning on posting changes the analysis sample after randomization.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 13 and 26, Tables 1 and 3; p. 24, Section 6; p. 56, Table 21. Counts calculated by subtraction.

confirmed.statement: S1 writing time uses 38,203 posts: 16,489 control and 21,714 treatment. Time is missing for timed-out sessions or closed/reopened browser windows; the resulting exclusions are 10,292 control and 10,000 treatment posts, derived from the posted-job totals.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 13, Table 1 and notes; p. 56, Table 21, Minutes spent on job post and Number of words rows. Exclusions calculated by subtraction.

confirmed.statement: S1 semantic similarity uses 32,513 post-level observations; the predicted-active-use similarity model uses 32,282. The form correctly flags the unexplained smaller samples, and neither table reports similarity-analysis arm counts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 47, Table 12 and notes; p. 18, Table 2 and notes; compare p. 13, Table 1 (58,495 posts).

confirmed.statement: Table 21 reports the S1 treatment opt-in mean as 0.752 over 27,111 records; this denominator is not the 90,048 assigned treatment accounts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 56, Table 21, Opt-in rate for AI feature and Job posting rate rows.

confirmed.statement: S2 reports 101,601 returning employers and 164,382 openings; the openings are repeated outputs. Both account-level analyses in Table 36 retain 101,601 observations, matching the allocation figure.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 66, Appendix B; p. 69, Figure 16; p. 72, Table 36.

confirmed.statement: S2 treatment categories are 27,192 opt-ins, 16,707 opt-outs, and 7,081 who never reached the choice. Their sum gives 50,980 treated accounts; subtracting from 101,601 gives 50,621 control accounts. These are derived account totals, not printed people counts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 71, Table 35 and notes; pp. 66 and 72, total experimental sample and Table 36. Arm totals derived by addition and subtraction.

confirmed.statement: S2 Table 37 restricts analysis to 43,899 opt-in/opt-out accounts (27,192 plus 16,707); the 7,081 first-stage drop-offs are not lost from Table 36's full account analysis. Table 36 excludes spam postings from its post-count outcome, not from its reported employer denominator.

S3 Figure 15 reports 525,119 new employers starting a post during October 10, 2023-February 18, 2024, with randomized 95% treatment and 5% control. Exact arm totals, distinct-person counts, and post-specific analysis counts are not supplied.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 37, Section 8; p. 68, Figure 15 and notes.

confirmed.statement: Table 11 pools the original experiment and later entrants, including the rollout: 1,033,681 account observations and 281,214 posted-job observations. These overlap S1 and S3 and cannot be added as another independent sample.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 38-40, Section 8, Figure 9 and Table 11 notes; p. 68, Figure 15 notes.

confirmed.statement: S4 is a self-selected editing comparison within S1 treatment opt-ins, with 13,107 posts for similarity and 20,024 observations for the other Table 15 outcomes. It adds no independent randomized participants; editing-arm people counts are not reported.
confirmed.locator: PDF pp. 15 and 17, Section 4.5.2; p. 50, Table 15 and notes.

confirmed.statement: S2 concerns earlier returning employers, S1 newly registered employers in June-July 2023, and S3 later new entrants. These recruitment definitions distinguish account cohorts but do not establish whether any individual operated accounts in multiple cohorts.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 9, Section 3; p. 66, Appendix B; p. 68, Figure 15 notes.

confirmed.statement: The paper identifies no external paper as reusing this experimental sample. Its comparison with Wiles, Munyikwa and Horton (2025) describes a different resume-editing intervention; absence of a shared-sample statement does not prove person-level non-overlap.
confirmed.locator: Full markdown, including references and Appendices A-B; particularly PDF p. 2, footnote 2, and p. 46, reference to Wiles, Munyikwa and Horton (2025).

confirmed.statement: The 480,951 jobseekers, 1,174,442 applications, and 67,682 distinct jobs in Section 6.5 describe downstream applicants and their repeated applications. These are not counts of employers randomized to AI-writing assistance.
confirmed.locator: PDF p. 30, Section 6.5 and Equation 3; p. 9, Section 3.

confirmed.statement: The saved form already uses null for every study and arm people count, counts_are other, and criterion 2 unclear. Its account/post counts checked above agree with the PDF; the positive eligibility assertion in the brief is stronger than the current form.
confirmed.locator: forms/c635.json, studies[S1-S4].participants, studies[S1-S4].arms, and eligibility; PDF locators given above.

summary: The positive conclusion that at least 50 people were analyzed is unsupported because the randomized samples count employer accounts without a verified count of distinct people. The current form already records null people counts and unclear eligibility, and its reported account and post counts were confirmed.
